overview: The City Council and Community Development Board reached consensus on building heights, boundaries, and student housing regulations for the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District zoning amendments. Both bodies voted to close the public hearing and scheduled a final working session for August to prepare formal recommendations.

items.title: Presentation on Proposed Student Housing Standards
items.summary: PDS Director Alicia Hunt presented proposed standards for purpose-built student housing, including a 150-bed minimum requirement, 24/7 professional management, and annual occupancy reviews.

items.title: Height Scenarios and Shadow Studies
items.summary: Innes Associates presented multiple height scenarios for sub-districts BA1, BA2, and BA3, accompanied by shadow studies modeling impact during February and June.

items.title: Public Hearing
items.summary: Residents and stakeholders provided testimony regarding building heights, traffic congestion on Boston Avenue, and the potential impact of private student housing on residential character.

items.title: Sub-District BA1 Heights and Boundaries
items.summary: Approved height Option A for BA1, setting the limit at three stories with a one-story incentive, and agreed to maintain the original sub-district boundaries without reductions.

items.title: Sub-District BA2 Heights and Setbacks
items.summary: Approved height Option C for BA2, featuring four stories with a three-story incentive in the center, and amended the proposal to include a deeper first-floor setback on Winchester Street.

items.title: Sub-District BA3 Heights
items.summary: Approved height Option A for BA3, establishing a base of five stories with a two-story incentive.

items.title: Purpose-Built Student Housing and Affordability Incentive
items.summary: Approved the definition for purpose-built student housing with enhanced management plan requirements and directed staff to resolve technical issues within the affordability incentive table.

items.title: Closing of Public Hearing and Next Steps
items.summary: Voted to close the public hearing and scheduled a Community Development Board working session for August 12 to finalize the formal recommendations to the City Council.
